ai.literal: Distress when-comes, laugh; it pressing-and-overcoming, that equal-thing is-not.
ai.translation: When distress comes, laugh; there is nothing like that laughter to press on and overcome it.
ai.modern: துன்பம் வரும்போது சிரிக்க வேண்டும்; அந்தத் துன்பத்தைத் தொடர்ந்து சென்று வெல்வதற்கு அந்தச் சிரிப்பை விடச் சிறந்த வழி வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises how to face adversity with courage and a positive attitude. When distress (இடுக்கண்) arrives, the poet instructs us to laugh (நகுக) rather than despair. Laughter here represents a state of mental strength, resilience, and unshakeable calm. The second line explains why: there is no weapon equal to that cheerful defiance (அஃது ஒப்பது இல்) to press on and overcome (அடுத்தூர்வது) the trouble itself. By meeting sorrow with a smile, one disarms the adversity and gains the strength to conquer it.

ai.literal: Flood-like resembling affliction, one who possesses wisdom, within the mind as he contemplates, will perish.
ai.translation: Afflictions as vast as a flood will perish the moment a wise person calmly contemplates them within their mind.
ai.modern: வெள்ளம் போன்ற பெரிய துன்பங்களும், அறிவுடையவன் தன் மனத்திற்குள் அவற்றை நினைத்து ஆராயும்போதே அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the power of wisdom in overcoming immense difficulties. The phrase 'வெள்ளத்து அனைய இடும்பை' compares overwhelming troubles to a vast, sweeping flood. However, for a wise person ('அறிவுடையான்'), these massive problems do not cause despair. Instead, as they calmly contemplate and analyze the situation within their mind ('உள்ளத்தின் உள்ள'), the power of the affliction vanishes ('கெடும்'). The couplet teaches that mental clarity and thoughtful reflection can dissolve even the most formidable challenges.

ai.literal: To affliction, affliction they will inflict, who to affliction do not suffer.
ai.translation: Those who do not lose heart and suffer when affliction comes will themselves inflict affliction upon that affliction.
ai.modern: துன்பம் வரும்போது அதற்காக வருந்தாதவர்கள், அந்தத் துன்பத்திற்கே துன்பத்தை உண்டாக்குவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of resilience in the face of adversity. The poet uses a powerful repetition of the word 'idumbai' (affliction) to illustrate a psychological triumph. When a person refuses to be broken or saddened by difficulties, they effectively disarm the trouble itself. Instead of the individual suffering, the distress is defeated and forced to retreat, meaning the resilient person inflicts suffering upon the suffering itself.

ai.literal: At all the places where obstructed, like a bull, he who is; the distress encountered by him will suffer distress.
ai.translation: Like a strong bull that pulls a cart through every obstacle, he who perseveres will cause distress itself to suffer distress.
ai.modern: தடைகள் ஏற்படும் இடங்களிலெல்லாம் வண்டியை இழுத்துச் செல்லும் எருதைப் போன்ற விடாமுயற்சி உடையவன் அடையும் துன்பமானது, அத்துன்பத்திற்கே துன்பத்தை உண்டாக்கிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a powerful agricultural metaphor to describe resilience. A strong draft bull (பகடு) does not stop when its cart gets stuck in mud or encounters obstacles (மடுத்த வாய் எல்லாம்); it exerts more strength and pulls through. A person who faces life's obstacles with the same relentless determination will find that the distress (இடுக்கண்) they encounter is itself defeated and made to suffer (இடர்ப்பாடு உடைத்து). Through this image, the poet shows that active perseverance turns the tables on adversity.

ai.literal: Even if they come piled up, the distress encountered by him who has no despair will itself suffer distress.
ai.translation: Even if troubles come crowding in waves, the distress met by a person who does not despair will itself suffer distress and flee.
ai.modern: துன்பங்கள் அடுக்கடுக்காக வந்தாலும், மனத்தளர்ச்சி இல்லாதவன் அடையும் துன்பமானது தானே துன்பப்பட்டு அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a powerful personification of distress to show the strength of resilience. The poet states that when a person of undaunted spirit, who refuses to sink into despair (அழிவிலான்), encounters difficulties, those difficulties cannot break him. Even if troubles pile up one after another (அடுக்கி வரினும்), the distress itself gets distressed (இடுக்கண் இடுக்கட்படும்) and is defeated by his unwavering courage. Ultimately, resilience turns the tables on adversity, making the trouble itself suffer failure.

ai.literal: Thinking 'we have lost everything', will they suffer grief, those who do not know how to hoard thinking 'we have obtained'?
ai.translation: Will those who do not know how to hoard and gloat when they gain something, ever suffer from grief when they lose it?
ai.modern: நாம் பெற்றுவிட்டோம் என்று எண்ணிக் காப்பாற்றி மகிழத் தெரியாதவர்கள், நாம் இழந்துவிட்டோம் என்று எண்ணித் துன்பப்படுவார்களா?
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the secret to remaining unaffected by adversity and loss. Those who do not get overly attached to gains, and do not spend their time anxiously hoarding or gloating over what they have acquired, will not feel devastated when those things are lost. Since they do not experience the high of possession, they are immune to the low of deprivation. True resilience comes from maintaining equanimity towards both gain and loss.

ai.literal: The target the body is for suffering, knowing this, distress as helplessness will indeed not adopt the noble.
ai.translation: Knowing that the body is but a target for suffering, the noble will not succumb to distress as if they are helpless.
ai.modern: உடம்பு துன்பத்திற்கு இலக்கு என்று உணர்ந்து, உயர்ந்த குணமுடையவர்கள் துன்பம் வரும்போது கலக்கத்தை ஒரு வழியாகக் கொள்ள மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how wise and noble people handle adversity. The body is naturally prone to physical and mental suffering; it is the very target ('இலக்கம்') at which suffering ('இடும்பை') aims. Knowing this fundamental truth, noble minds ('மேல்') do not allow distress ('கலக்கம்') to paralyze them or treat it as a state of helplessness ('கையாறு'). Instead of being overwhelmed, they accept adversity as a natural part of existence and maintain their composure.

ai.literal: He who does not desire pleasure, and says affliction is nature, experiencing sorrow he does not have.
ai.translation: He who does not long for pleasure and considers suffering to be natural will never experience sorrow.
ai.modern: இன்பத்தை விரும்பாதவனாய், துன்பம் என்பது வாழ்க்கையின் இயல்பான ஒன்று என்று கருதுபவன், துன்பமடைவது இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how to remain unaffected by adversity. The author states that a person who does not crave or chase after pleasure, and who accepts that suffering is a natural part of life, will never feel the sting of sorrow. By expecting difficulties as a normal occurrence rather than an anomaly, one builds mental resilience. Thus, when hardships inevitably arrive, they do not cause distress to such a balanced mind.

ai.literal: He who does not desire pleasure within pleasure, does not have the experiencing of pain within pain.
ai.translation: He who does not crave pleasure when experiencing pleasure, will not suffer from pain when experiencing pain.
ai.modern: இன்பம் வந்தபோது அந்த இன்பத்தை விரும்பி ஏங்காதவன், துன்பம் வந்தபோது அந்தத் துன்பத்தை அடைந்து வருந்த மாட்டான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the power of equanimity in overcoming life's hardships. The poet explains that a person who does not get overly attached to or crave pleasure during prosperous times remains emotionally balanced. Because they do not lose themselves in joy, they do not get crushed by sorrow when difficult times arrive. By maintaining a steady mind through both ups and downs, one becomes immune to the suffering caused by adversity.

ai.literal: If one takes pain as pleasure, there will become one's own enemies desiring greatness.
ai.translation: If a person accepts adversity as pleasure, they will attain a greatness that even their enemies will admire.
ai.modern: துன்பத்தை இன்பமாக ஏற்றுக்கொண்டால், ஒருவனுடைய பகைவரும் விரும்பத்தக்க பெருமை அவனுக்கு உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how to overcome adversity by changing one's attitude towards it. If a person welcomes difficulties and pain (இன்னாமை) as if they were pleasures (இன்பம்), they develop an unshakeable strength. This attitude leads to a level of greatness and distinction (சிறப்பு) that even their enemies (ஒன்னார்) will look upon with admiration and desire to possess. By not being defeated by suffering, one wins the ultimate respect of all.
